source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Mechanical V8, p.6-32

procedures.title: Rear main bearing oil seal (V8): replace
steps: Take out the upper half by tapping one end with a brass pin punch and small hammer until it sticks out far enough to grab with pliers (see figure 10V in the manual).

Oil the lip of the new upper half (not the parting-line faces) and push it gradually into place with a hammer handle while turning the crankshaft, rolling it in like a main bearing; do not let the tangs cut the back of the seal.
Put sealer at the parting line on the cap half.
Install the rear main cap with its new seal and torque to specifications.

procedures.title: Torsional damper (V8): remove
steps: Remove the fan belt, fan and pulley (Section 6K).
Remove the radiator and shroud (Section 13); on 427 Corvettes this is not needed unless more work such as camshaft removal is planned.
Corvette 427: remove the front engine mount through-bolts and raise the front of the engine until the damper clears the frame crossmember.
Remove the accessory drive pulley, then the damper retaining bolt if fitted.
Attach Tool J-6978 to the damper and turn the puller screw to draw it off (see figure 11V in the manual).

procedures.title: Torsional damper (V8): install, 307/327/350 except 302 and 327 325/350 hp
steps: Oil the front cover seal contact surface on the damper.
Attach installer J-22197 and tighten its fingers so the weight cannot move (see figure 12V in the manual).
Set the damper on the crankshaft and drive it on until it bottoms against the crankshaft sprocket, then remove the tool.
Install the radiator and shroud (Section 13) and the fan pulley and fan (Section 6K).
Install the fan belt and set its tension with a strand tension gauge.
Fill the cooling system, start the engine and check for leaks.
notes: CAUTION: always use the installer tool so the inertia weight cannot walk off the hub during installation.

procedures.title: Torsional damper (V8): install, 396 and 427
steps: Oil the front cover seal contact surface on the damper.
